title: Cauchy maps into complete normed fields converge
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative real absolute value, with distance $d(x,y)=|x-y|$ and its induced uniformity, and assume $F$ is complete. Let $J$ be a set, $\mathcal F$ a proper filter on $J$ (a family of subsets closed under finite intersections and passage to supersets, containing $J$ and not containing the empty set), and $u:J\to F$ a map. The image filter $u_*\mathcal F$ is Cauchy if and only if there exists $a\in F$ such that $u_*\mathcal F\leq\mathcal N(a)$, that is, $u$ converges to $a$ along $\mathcal F$. Here Cauchy means that for every $\epsilon>0$ some $S\in\mathcal F$ satisfies $|u(s)-u(t)|<\epsilon$ for all $s,t\in S$. In particular this applies to the tail filter of any net indexed by a nonempty directed set.
